title: The Problem of Identity and Change: Ship of Theseus
text:
The classic paradox of the Ship of Theseus questions whether an object remains fundamentally the same after all of its constituent parts have been replaced. If every plank, sail, and mast of a renowned vessel are gradually swapped out over time with new materials, one must ask at what point the original entity ceases to exist.

This philosophical quandary serves as a model for understanding persistence, requiring consideration of whether identity relies on material continuity, structural form, or functional pattern. It challenges common-sense notions of sameness across temporal durations, suggesting that 'identity' may be less an inherent property and more a conceptual construct.
